title: Diabetes mellitus: type, complications and medication status
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM codes for the patient's diabetes, its complications and related long-term drug use.
note:
Chief Complaint: Follow-up for diabetes management.

HPI: Patient is an 88-year-old female with a history of type 2 diabetes. She has been managed with an oral hypoglycemic agent for several years. She reports occasional fatigue but denies any acute changes in vision or sensation.
(Copied forward from prior visit): Patient reports adherence to medication. She notes that her blood glucose readings have been elevated recently. She denies any significant weight changes or acute illnesses.

Vitals: BP 128/82, HR 74, SpO2 98% on room air, Temp 98.6F, Weight 145 lbs.

Review of Systems:
Constitutional: Negative for fever, chills, or weight loss.
Cardiovascular: Negative for chest pain or palpitations.
Respiratory: Negative for shortness of breath or cough.
Neurological: Negative for dizziness or syncope.
Genitourinary: Negative for dysuria.

Medication List:
Metformin 500mg PO BID

Exam:
General: Alert and oriented x3, in no acute distress.
Skin: No new lesions or rashes noted.
Extremities: No edema, pulses palpable.

Assessment:
Type 2 diabetes mellitus.
Hyperglycemia.

Plan:
Continue current metformin regimen. Patient advised to monitor home glucose readings more frequently. Follow up in 3 months.

Electronically signed, 
L. Moreau, NP
October 14, 2026
explanations: Diabetes documented as poorly controlled, out of control, or with hyperglycemia is coded to diabetes with hyperglycemia.
Long-term oral hypoglycemic use: add Z79.84.

distractors.why: Hyperglycemia is a complication with its own code.
Z79.84 captures long-term oral hypoglycemic use.
